note: THE DESK-SIDE CONTROL for 201/9-01's sprite change, and NOT a device row. The phone has no `timestamp-query`, so on the device a blit is priced by flying `nosprites` against `board` — which needs a settled window and a thermal bracket. This answers the narrower question at a desk: is a blit cheaper than rebuilding the path at all, and by how much. Its second reading is the one that mattered: it puts a SCALE under the device's number.
how: scripts/debug/canvas-symbol-arms.mjs — headless Chromium, a real Canvas2D at 720x640, 150 marks a frame drawn both ways. Arms interleaved (path, blit, path, blit) and run twice per invocation; the whole thing run three times.
why: apps/dispatch/src/map/symbol-sprites.ts bakes each mark once and blits it per instance instead of tessellating and filling its path every frame — MapLibre's icon atlas and deck.gl's IconLayer, taken for their reason rather than by analogy.

instrument.clamp: `performance.now()` is clamped to ~100 us in a browser, and one frame of 150 marks is 0.3 ms — three ticks. The FIRST version of this measurement timed single frames, and every sample quantized onto 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.5 so the arms overlapped on the mean while the p50 stayed one tick apart. Not a measurement.
instrument.fix: a sample is a BLOCK of 40 frames, divided back down — two orders above the clamp.
instrument.reading: the block form is what the numbers below come from; the single-frame form is recorded here because it looked like a clean 15 % result and was not.

device: desk container, headless Chromium /opt/pw-browsers/chromium — NOT the 2/03 phone

reading.verdict: the blit arm is the cheaper of the two in every one of the three paired invocations, ~0.275 ms against ~0.32 ms for 150 marks — roughly 10-20 %, or 0.03-0.06 ms a frame at this count.
reading.smallPrint: the path arm's SECOND sample is consistently below its first (0.3425 -> 0.300, 0.35 -> 0.305, 0.3425 -> 0.305) while the blit arm does not move, so the honest comparison is against path's warmed sample and the win is at the low end of that range.
reading.theOtherFinding: 150 marks cost ~0.3 ms HERE while the phone reports `overlay:symbols` at 7.37 ms at 192 symbols. Even at a 10x device penalty that leaves most of the span unexplained, so on the phone the DRAWING is a minority of that line and the next place to look is everything else the layer does per unit — two projections, a colour string, a cache key, a hit-area object and a rank object, 150 times a frame.

owed: the device arm. `?sprites=0` and the panel's `nosprites` link exist for it; the panel process has to be restarted before it serves the new link table.

theScaleBar.question: `sym:scale` measures ~250 us a frame on the device for ONE scale bar — a third of what forty calls cost — and the obvious explanation was the two `ctx.font` assignments it makes, since this layer's oldest note is that assigning the font re-parses the shorthand.
theScaleBar.verdict: REFUTED as an absolute explanation. Alternating two shorthands costs 0.6 us an assignment against 0.1 for repeating one — so the churn IS ~6x, exactly as the note says, and it is 1.2 us a frame. The WHOLE bar, font churn included, is 3 us.
theScaleBar.whatItLeaves: the device spends ~250 us on 3 us of desk work — the same ~80x ratio `sym:units` carried before its allocations were removed. Two candidates and only the device can separate them: (a) font handling really is that much more expensive on this phone, which its own history supports (`overlay:clear` was 212 ms before `warmTextMetrics` landed, and font resolution was the cause); (b) the span instrument itself, since `sym:scale` wraps the least work of the four `sym:*` spans — though `overlay:sketches` reads 0.03-0.06 ms in the same captures, which puts the floor below that and makes (b) the weaker of the two.
theScaleBar.doNotShipTheGuess: no change was made. A ~1 % micro-fix on a refuted inference, unmeasurable from here, is what this session learned twice not to do.
